title: feat: key quest rewards on the GitHub user id
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Splits the reward-keying and database migration out of #13471 so the anti-abuse foundation can be reviewed and deployed independently. #13471 is stacked on this PR and contains the account-settings and deletion UI.

- Adds a shared `rewardKey()` so quest checks and admin grants use `quest:{questId}:github:{githubId}` consistently.
- Makes `user.github_id` unique so one GitHub identity cannot hold two active accounts.
- Makes `rewards.user_id` nullable with `ON DELETE SET NULL`, allowing the reward idempotency record to survive account deletion without retaining the deleted user row.
- Drops the redundant `rewards.github_id` column; the GitHub identity is already encoded in the idempotency key.
- Keeps replacement accounts from earning the same quest again. Quest status remains scoped to the current account, so a replacement account sees the quest as open, but recording the reward is a no-op because the GitHub-scoped key already exists.
- Keeps orphaned rewards out of the leaderboard.
- Updates community-endpoint tests so coexisting approved owners use distinct allowlisted GitHub IDs under the new uniqueness constraint.

## Migrations

`0050` is a custom Drizzle migration that re-keys `quest:{id}:user:{userId}` rows to `quest:{id}:github:{githubId}` while the existing unique index is still present. A collision therefore aborts before schema changes are applied.

`0051` is generated by Drizzle and makes the schema changes: unique `user.github_id`, nullable `rewards.user_id`, and removal of `rewards.github_id`.

**Deploy the migrations before the Worker.** The new code writes GitHub-scoped keys that depend on the migrated schema and data.

## Verification

Production data checks found 19,242 rewards, 18,889 quest rewards eligible for re-keying, 353 issue-bounty keys left unchanged, 0 duplicate GitHub IDs, 0 accounts without a GitHub ID, 0 key collisions, and 0 rewards referencing a deleted user. The migrations were replayed from the full migration history. Quest tests,

gist.headline: One Bee, One Bloom
gist.blurb: Quest rewards now remember the GitHub gardener behind the account. Delete, replace, return — a completed bloom stays completed, without leaving old account rows tangled in the roots.
gist.summary: Quest reward idempotency is now keyed as `quest:{questId}:github:{githubId}`, with unique `user.github_id` and deletion-safe reward records so each GitHub identity can earn a quest reward once across account replacements.
gist.impact: Quest participants get durable, GitHub-scoped reward history: replacement accounts can still view available quests, while previously completed rewards remain safely recorded and orphaned records stay off the leaderboard.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy quest garden where Polli uses a GitHub-shaped brass key to label one flowering reward plant, while an old empty pot is gently removed without disturbing the flower's record plaque. The visual metaphor is that rewards belong to a stable GitHub identity rather than a disposable account pot; include subtle terminal labels for `github_id` and a tidy leaderboard sign.
